contentHtml:
Lights that come on as you pull into the drive, a front door you can unlock from your phone, and one "goodnight" that locks up and switches everything off. I set up smart home automation across Stretton and Brisbane and make the pieces actually work together, so it feels effortless instead of a drawer full of half-working gadgets.

Smart gadgets are easy to buy and hard to make work

Most people's smart home is a light here, a plug there, three different apps, and half of it forgotten because it kept dropping off the wi-fi. The devices are the easy bit. Getting them onto a reliable network, into one app, and set up so they trigger each other on their own is where it comes good, and where most DIY setups fall apart. I am an IT technician first, so the network underneath is solid before a single automation goes on top.

Google, Alexa or Apple, one system your way

If you already talk to Google, Alexa or Siri, I build your smart home around that one and get everything playing nicely with it. No more three apps for three brands, just one place to control the lot and a voice assistant that does what you ask. Already started and hit a wall? Sorting out half-finished smart homes is one of my most common jobs.

What I set up

  • Smart lighting that dims, schedules, and comes on at sunset or when you arrive. One tap or one word for movie night or dinner.
  • Smart locks and video doorbells, unlock from your phone, hand out a temporary guest code, and see and talk to whoever is at the door from anywhere.
  • Voice control for lights, music, timers and blinds through Google, Alexa or Siri, set up to respond the way you expect.
  • Climate and comfort, run the air-con and fans from your phone or a schedule, so the house is right when you get home and off when nobody is in.
  • Smart plugs and power, turn anything into a smart device, schedule the pool pump or heater, and see what is quietly running up the power bill.
  • Sensors and routines, motion, door and leak sensors that tie into automations, so the house reacts on its own.

Works with your cameras and alarm

Automation is far more useful when it talks to your security. I can link your smart home in with your CCTV cameras and alarm, so lights come on when a camera spots movement and you get the whole picture in one app. It all rides on a proper home network, which is why I sort the wireless network first.

Send me the details for a quote or call 0477 319 160, with no call-out fee anywhere on Stretton.
